findings.title: T7 precedence list contradicts its own required TIGHTEN behaviour
findings.description:
T7 says to implement the bands "exactly, in this precedence order", with step 1 `n < floor → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`. Step 4, the next sub-item and T8 then require a below-floor, low-match cell to return `TIGHTEN`. A literal implementation of the numbered order fails T8 line 134.

Two cases are also undefined:
- **Unversioned and low match rate:** step 2 returns `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, but "tightening is not gated" suggests `TIGHTEN`.
- **Below floor and mid-band:** presumably `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, but not stated.

Fix: reorder to (1) `match_rate <= tighten_rate` → `TIGHTEN`, (2) `n < floor` or unversioned → `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, (3) `match_rate >= graduate_rate` → `GRADUATE`, (4) `HOLD`. State the unversioned-and-low decision explicitly and add it to T8's parametrisation.

findings.title: T13 leaves result discovery, lapse signal, pruned-file handling and rounding undecided
findings.description:
Four things the success criteria depend on are left to the implementer:

- **Result discovery.** T13 says to reuse 320's result-discovery surface "if one exists", else scope to store-recorded samples only, or ask the Project Manager. `MetrologyStore` (`src/squadron/metrology/store.py:131-195`) exposes only sample records. Samples are by definition already sampled, so that fallback can never yield an unsampled result and the "non-empty offer set" criterion goes unmet. The PM-wait branch is also invalid under project rules. The task must name the concrete discovery function (I did not check what `capture.resolve_target` enumerates) or add an explicit sub-task to build it.
- **Lapse signal.** The return type is fixed as `list[OfferTarget]`, yet T13 says to "return enough information (or have the CLI re-derive it)" and T14 asserts on "whatever signal T13 produces". Pick one shape, for example a result model carrying offers plus per-graduation status (current, exhausted or lapsed).
- **Pruned review file.** T14 line 218 tests "skipped, counted, WARNING", but T13 has no implementation item for it and `list[OfferTarget]` has nowhere to carry a count.
- **Rate rounding.** At a small rate over few results (say 0.1 over 3), floor rounding gives zero offers and breaks the guarantee. T13 must state the rule (for example ceiling, minimum one when any unsampled match exists) and T14 must test a small-rate case.

findings.title: Idempotent re-graduate has no store primitive to implement it
findings.description:
T15 requires "update its evidence snapshot in place (one record, not two)". T11 provides only `write_graduation`, which returns a freshly generated id, and `find_graduation`, which returns a `GraduatedConfig` with no record id. The store has no update path and keys files by id (`_record_path`).

As tasked, T15 must either write a second record (failing T16 line 246) or invent store work inside the CLI shell. Add to T11 either a deterministic record id derived from `(JudgeConfigId, artifact_level)` so a rewrite overwrites, or an explicit upsert method. Move the single-record test into T12.

findings.title: T11 creates a circular import and blurs which module owns what
findings.description:
`JudgeConfigId` lives in `models.py`. T3 puts `GraduatedConfig` in `calibration_models.py`, which must import `JudgeConfigId` from `models.py`. T11 then adds `graduated_config: GraduatedConfig | None` to `MetrologyRecord` in `models.py`, so the two modules import each other. Pydantic needs the real type at validation time, so a `TYPE_CHECKING` guard will not do.

T11 is also headed "Add `graduation.py`" while its items edit `models.py` and `store.py`. `write_graduation(store, graduated)` is described both as a module function and as a "method on `MetrologyStore`".

Fix: define `GraduatedConfig` and `EvidenceSnapshot` in `models.py` (or name another cycle-free placement), and state for each function whether it is a store method or a `graduation.py` function.

findings.title: Runtime-drawn-model limitation is not in the note text or any assertion
findings.description:
The success criterion requires the runtime-drawn-model limitation to be "stated where the recommendation is produced (asserted: the note is present in output, including `--json`)".

T9 specifies only the "this template paired with this model, choose together at config time" half of `model_dimension_note`. The statement that a pool-drawn step's threshold cannot track the drawn model is absent. T10 and T16 assert only that the note is non-empty.

Add the limitation to T9's required content. Assert it in T10 and in T16's `--json` case against a shared constant, not a copied literal.

findings.title: Malformed `judge:` block row is claimed covered but is not
findings.description:
The Coverage Check (task file line 287) says this row is "inherited from `resolve_thresholds`, exercised in T8". Neither holds:
- `resolve_thresholds` calls `float()` on the value, so a non-numeric floor raises `ValueError`. That contradicts T7's "never raises".
- T8 contains no malformed-block test.

The design's Failure Modes row requires a flagged target, a WARNING naming the template, and a test. Add a T7 item to catch the specific `ValueError`/`TypeError`, log the WARNING and return `None`, plus a T8 case.

findings.title: Config key defaults are never specified
findings.description:
T5's success criterion needs `sq config list` to show defaults, and T6 asserts "correct types and defaults". Neither the task file nor the slice design gives a value for `graduate_match_rate`, `tighten_match_rate` or `residual_sample_rate`. Existing keys all carry explicit defaults (`src/squadron/config/keys.py:144-152`).

The implementer would have to invent the thresholds that drive every recommendation. State the three values in T5. Also say whether `tighten_match_rate >= graduate_match_rate` is rejected.

findings.title: Commit markers follow every task, including untested implementation
findings.description:
All 17 tasks end with a commit line, so every implementation task (T1, T3, T5, T7, T9, T11, T13, T15) commits before its tests exist. T1 in particular changes the hash with no accompanying test.

The markers are also written `**Commit:**` (colon inside the bold) instead of the `**Commit**:` convention, so tooling may not recognise them.

Fix: one marker per implementation-and-test pair (after T2, T4, T6, T8, T10, T12, T14, T16, T17), in the `**Commit**:` form.

findings.title: Task file is heavier than a 3/5 slice needs
findings.description:
The file has 17 tasks, six new test files and two extended ones. Suggested cuts and merges:

- **T6 into T5:** three key registrations do not need a standalone test task.
- **T4 into T3:** it mostly tests Pydantic round-tripping, which no success criterion requires. Keep only the `template_content_hash` and `current=None` assertions.
- **No-mutation check:** it is tested at T10, T16 and T17 step 4. The criterion is stated at the `recommend` level, so keep T16 and drop T10's copy.
- **`test_calibration_recommend.py`:** fold it into `test_calibration.py`.

That leaves about 13 tasks with no loss of criterion coverage.

findings.title: `graduate` pairing lookup can match more than one cell
findings.description: After a prompt edit, filtering recommendations by `--template/--model/--level` can match two cells (old hash and new hash). T15 does not say which is "current". Specify that `graduate` matches the cell whose `template_content_hash` equals the currently registered template's hash.

findings.title: Exhausted-config "no offers due" line is not exercised at the CLI
findings.description: T15 and T16 cover the lapsed explanatory line. The design's separate "no offers due" line for an exhausted but current config has no T15 render item and no T16 case. One line in each closes it.

findings.title: Success criteria trace to tasks; no scope creep
findings.description:
Each criterion has a task:
- **Hash narrowing, both directions:** T1/T2.
- **Floor and unversioned refusal:** T7/T8.
- **Advisory, no mutation:** T9, T16.
- **Version-scoped graduation:** T11–T14.
- **Residual offers:** T13/T14.
- **CLI:** T15/T16.
- **Surface-agnostic core:** T16.
- **300/320/321 unchanged, pyright and ruff clean:** T17.

No task falls outside the slice. Deferred items are correctly absent, and no merge or push is written as a task.

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with pattern
findings.description: Hash fix comes first, config keys are moved ahead of the core that reads them, and models precede their consumers. Every implementation task is immediately followed by its test task. There are no dependency cycles between tasks; the module-level import cycle is covered above.

findings.title: No load test or CI wiring required
findings.description: The slice restates no latency, throughput or resource requirement. It touches only local-filesystem, synchronous paths, so the absence of a `tests/load/` task and CI gate is correct.
